name: What If You Change Tile or Fixtures After the Remodel Starts?

mainEntity.name: What happens if I change my mind on tile or fixtures after the bathroom remodel starts?
mainEntity.text: What happens if I change my mind on tile or fixtures after the bathroom remodel starts?

acceptedAnswer.text: If you change your mind after the remodel starts, expect cost and schedule impacts. Tile, fixtures, vanities, and glass are often ordered in advance, and late changes can create restocking fees, extra labor, or delays while replacement items are sourced. The contractor may need to stop work until the new selection arrives, especially if the item affects layout or installation details. That is why finalizing materials before construction starts is so important. A good contract should explain how substitutions, upgrades, and cancellations are handled. Ask the contractor what selections must be locked before demolition and which items can still be changed later without major disruption. If you are undecided, it is better to choose flexible, widely available products rather than specialty items with long lead times. Late changes are common, but they are easiest to manage when the process and pricing rules are clear from the beginning.
acceptedAnswer.description: If you change selections after work starts, the contractor will usually issue a change order for added labor, restocking fees, delays, or wasted materials. The earlier you finalize choices, the less expensive and disruptive the changes are. A good contract should explain how substitutions and upgrades are priced.
